causal_assumptions.consistency: Conditions follow the reported parent, researcher, and alone protocols.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported by random assignment, subject to attrition and protocol adherence.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Participants were assigned across all three conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Randomized parent-buffer versus comparison-condition difference in the post-stressor cortisol trajectory.

confidence.rationale: Random assignment supports a causal protocol contrast, but a standardized effect estimate was not extracted.

limitations: The condition contrast does not identify a unique social-buffering mechanism.

boundary_conditions: Does not automatically generalize to adults
scope.population: 180 children aged 11 to 15 years in the MISTiC experiment.
scope.temporal_scope: Baseline through repeated samples up to 65 minutes after baseline.

claims.statement: In the MISTiC trial, random assignment to the parent-buffer condition changed the cortisol stress-response trajectory relative to researcher-buffer and no-buffer conditions.
claims.temporal_ordering: Condition assignment and buffer interactions preceded post-stressor cortisol sampling.

confidence.rationale: The trial reported a condition-by-trial interaction and post-hoc contrasts, but no standardized interaction estimate was extracted.

interaction_term.notes: Reported p < .05; parent condition differed from both comparison conditions.

limitations: Statistical moderation does not by itself establish causal effect modification or mediation.

boundary_conditions: The interaction is scale- and model-dependent and is not a mediating mechanism.
scope.population: 180 children aged 11 to 15 years in the MISTiC experiment.
scope.temporal_scope: Repeated baseline and post-stressor saliva samples.

claims.statement: In the MISTiC trial, randomized buffer condition statistically modified change in cortisol across sampling trials.

confidence.rationale: Support condition was randomized and the group interaction was reported, but developmental history was observational.

interaction_term.notes: Parent support dampened cortisol relative to stranger support in nonadopted children but not in postinstitutionalized children.

limitations: The interaction is not proof of a specific developmental mechanism.

boundary_conditions: Group differences cannot be attributed uniquely to institutional care because developmental history was not randomized.
scope.population: 40 postinstitutionalized and 40 age- and gender-matched nonadopted children aged approximately 9 to 11 years.
scope.temporal_scope: Cortisol response to a modified TSST following randomized speech-preparation support.

claims.statement: In Hostinar et al., the parent-versus-stranger support contrast differed between nonadopted and postinstitutionalized children.

confidence.rationale: Randomized condition effects establish protocol effects, while the proposed co-regulatory process was not uniquely manipulated or measured.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The hypothesis is weakened if matched familiar support repeatedly fails to alter candidate appraisal or regulation processes despite reliable cortisol effects.

boundary_conditions: Does not claim one neural mediator or universal benefit from any social contact.
scope.population: Children and adolescents represented by the two included experiments.
scope.temporal_scope: Support interaction before or during acute social-evaluative stress.

claims.statement: Familiar-support co-regulation may contribute to reduced cortisol responding, with effectiveness conditional on developmental and relationship context.
claims.temporal_ordering: Support interaction occurs before the measured post-stressor cortisol trajectory.

evidence.design: Three-arm randomized MISTiC experiment with parent, researcher, and no-buffer conditions.

effect.metric: randomized condition contrast in cortisol trajectory
effect.notes: Parent condition differed from both comparison conditions.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, randomized conditions and cortisol post-hoc contrasts.
limitations: Numerical standardized effect and full risk-of-bias assessment remain pending.
evidence.summary: Random assignment identifies a study-protocol effect on cortisol trajectory under stated assumptions.

evidence.design: Repeated cortisol sampling analyzed with sampling-trial by randomized-condition interaction.
limitations: The interaction does not identify a mediator.
evidence.summary: Cortisol change across trials differed statistically by assigned buffer condition.

evidence.design: Randomized parent-versus-stranger speech-preparation support, stratified by observational developmental-history group.

effect.notes: Selective parent buffering appeared in nonadopted but not postinstitutionalized children.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, support-condition by group interaction.
limitations: The moderator was not randomized and may bundle multiple developmental differences.
evidence.population: 80 children, equally divided between postinstitutionalized adoptees and matched nonadopted children.
evidence.summary: The randomized support contrast varied across an observational developmental-history grouping.

evidence.design: Mechanistic interpretation of support-condition differences across developmental-history groups.

effect.notes: Familiarity-selective buffering varied by developmental group; the process was not directly measured.

limitations: Post hoc mechanism interpretation from outcome contrasts.
evidence.population: 80 children in the Hostinar et al. experiment.
evidence.summary: The pattern is compatible with context-sensitive co-regulation but does not identify its implementation.

metadata.description: Separates randomized support conditions, developmental context, cortisol trajectories, statistical moderation, causal contrasts, and proposed co-regulation.
metadata.title: Primary evidence pack for social buffering of cortisol stress responses

objects.definition: Randomized protocol condition providing parent interaction or support around a social-evaluative stressor.
objects.delivery: Study-specific brief parent interaction before or during stress preparation.
objects.label: Parent social-buffer condition

objects.definition: Randomized researcher, stranger, or no-buffer condition defined by the source study.

objects.label: Serial salivary cortisol

objects.label: Social co-regulation of stress responding

Relationship and developmental context permit effective co-regulation.
